seoTitle: Can You Integrate Square with Squarespace as a Payment Option?
metaDescription: Square isn't a selectable payment processor on Squarespace's website checkout. Here's where the Payments setting actually lives, and how Square really connects through Point of Sale.
intro: Searching for a way to add Square as a payment option on a Squarespace store usually ends at the same wall: Settings → Selling → Payments simply doesn't list it. That's not a bug or a hidden toggle. Squarespace Commerce supports only three processors for online checkout — Squarespace Payments, Stripe, and PayPal — and Square isn't one of them. This guide shows that Payments screen so you can see the real options, then covers the one place Square does connect to Squarespace: Point of Sale, for in-person sales.
prerequisites: A Squarespace Commerce plan — Point of Sale and payment processing aren't available on Squarespace's non-Commerce plans
For in-person Square payments specifically: an existing Square account and a supported Square Reader
costNote: Square's own point-of-sale processing rates apply whenever Square is your in-person payment processor; Squarespace doesn't add a markup on top. Point of Sale itself requires a Commerce plan, and the physical Square Reader Squarespace sells is available only to merchants in the US.

steps.heading: Log into your Squarespace account
steps.body: Head to the Squarespace login screen and sign in with your email and password, or use one of the Continue with Google, Apple, or Facebook options if that's how your account was originally set up. Once you're in, Squarespace takes you to your dashboard, where you'll pick the specific site you want to work with if you manage more than one.

image.caption: The Squarespace login screen, with email/password sign-in alongside Google, Apple, and Facebook options.

steps.heading: Open your site dashboard and find Settings
steps.body: From your site's home panel, which shows a Get started checklist, your site preview, and links like Manage Domain and Publish Your Site, look at the left-hand navigation. Website, Products & Services, Scheduling, and Invoicing all sit here, but the setting you need is reached through the gear icon at the bottom of the sidebar, labeled Settings.

image.caption: A Squarespace site dashboard, with the Settings gear icon at the bottom of the left sidebar.

steps.heading: Open Selling, then Payments, and see what's actually listed
steps.body: Inside Settings, the left column lists categories including Website, Domains & Email, Customer Notifications, Selling, Brand, Marketing, Third Party Tools, and Billing. Click Selling, then Payments. This is where every online checkout processor gets connected, and according to Squarespace's own support documentation, that list holds exactly three names: Squarespace Payments, Stripe, and PayPal. Square isn't among them and never has been; Squarespace Commerce doesn't support it for online checkout.

image.caption: The Selling settings page, with Payments highlighted among Business Information, Customer Accounts, Low Stock Alerts, Cart, and Checkout.

steps.heading: For Square specifically, that's Point of Sale, not this page
steps.body: Square connects to Squarespace through a separate feature: Point of Sale, built into the Squarespace app for taking in-person payments. There, you can choose Squarespace Payments, Stripe, or Square as the processor for a physical sale, and inventory syncs back to your online store automatically. It needs a supported Square Reader connected to the app; Squarespace explicitly doesn't support the Square Register, Stand, or Terminal. Point of Sale itself works in the US and UK, but the Square Reader hardware Squarespace sells ships only to US merchants, so UK sellers would pair Point of Sale with a different processor.

steps.heading: If online checkout was the actual goal, connect Stripe or PayPal instead
steps.body: Back on the Payments page from step three, click Connect beneath Stripe or PayPal (or set up Squarespace Payments, where available) and follow the prompts to authorize that account. Once connected, it shows up as an active method on the Payments settings page. Visit your storefront's checkout and either place a small test order or confirm the processor appears as a selectable option, before announcing the change anywhere. Payment settings are exactly the kind of setting where a small misconfiguration only becomes obvious the moment a real customer tries to check out.

troubleshooting.problem: Square doesn't appear when I open Settings → Selling → Payments
troubleshooting.cause: Square was never supported as an online checkout processor. That list only ever shows Squarespace Payments, Stripe, and PayPal.
troubleshooting.fix: Pick one of those three for website checkout. If Square specifically matters, use it through Point of Sale in the Squarespace app for in-person sales instead.

troubleshooting.problem: The Square Reader won't pair inside the Squarespace app
troubleshooting.cause: Only the Square Reader itself is supported, not Square's Register, Stand, or Terminal hardware, and Squarespace sells the reader only to US merchants.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm you're using a genuine Square Reader. Outside the US, pair Point of Sale with a different supported processor instead.

troubleshooting.problem: Point of Sale doesn't show up in my account at all
troubleshooting.cause: It requires a Commerce plan, and per Squarespace's own documentation, it's limited to businesses in the US and UK.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your current plan under Settings → Billing, and confirm your business is registered in a supported country.

faq.question: Can I add Square as an online payment option on my Squarespace store?
faq.answer: No. Squarespace's own support documentation lists only three processors for online checkout: Squarespace Payments, Stripe, and PayPal. Square has never been one of them.

faq.question: How do I actually accept Square payments through Squarespace, then?
faq.answer: Through Point of Sale, a feature in the Squarespace app for in-person sales. There you can pick Square as your processor for a physical transaction, and the sale syncs back to your online store's inventory.

faq.question: Which processors can I use for online checkout on Squarespace?
faq.answer: Squarespace Payments, Stripe, and PayPal. You connect any of them from Settings → Selling → Payments.

faq.question: Is Squarespace Point of Sale available everywhere?
faq.answer: Point of Sale works in the US and UK, but the physical Square Reader Squarespace sells is only available to merchants in the US. UK sellers use Point of Sale with a different processor.

faq.question: What fees does Square charge through Squarespace's Point of Sale?
faq.answer: Square's own standard point-of-sale processing rates, the same as using a Square Reader anywhere else. Squarespace doesn't add its own fee on top, though refunds don't return the original Square transaction fee.

faq.question: Will my existing Squarespace payment methods still work if I connect another one?
faq.answer: Yes. Any processor you connect on the Payments page is added alongside whatever you already have enabled, so customers choose from all active methods at checkout.

verifiedNote: The login, dashboard, and Selling settings screens come from a recorded walkthrough. The earlier draft of this article described selecting Square directly on the online Payments page and authorizing it for checkout — checked against three official Squarespace support articles in September 2026, that flow doesn't exist. Squarespace Commerce supports Squarespace Payments, Stripe, and PayPal for online checkout; Square connects only through the separate Point of Sale feature for in-person sales. This version was rewritten around that correction.
